But you've seen no evidence of that?
Not yet. What I do know is that the Captain of this ship has just gone through an extreme physical transformation... the ultimate effects of which I can't even begin to guess.
You are asking me to step down.
There is a quiet beat before Beverly replies.
You're still Jean-Luc Picard... what do you think you should do?
As Young Picard thinks over the stakes involved...
As before. Young Picard and Beverly ENTER from the Ready Room. He goes directly to Riker and there is no trace of hesitation or regret at his decision.
Commander Riker, please take command of the ship until further notice.
Understood, sir.
And with that, Young Picard and Beverly head for the EXIT.
Young Ro and Young Guinan ENTER from Sickbay. Young Ro is very irritated as they pause in the Corridor.
So what the hell am I supposed to do now?
You're not supposed to do anything. That's what "relieved of duty" means.
Young Guinan looks up at the ceiling... jumps up and tries to touch it, but can't. She smiles in delight.
Well, I should be doing something... instead of just standing around waiting for them to find a cure.
You're right. Let's go play.
What?
I haven't been young for a long time... and I intend to enjoy every minute of it.
Fine. Enjoy yourself.
Young Ro heads down the Corridor toward a Turbolift.
What are you going to do... go back to your room and pout?
Young Ro stops dead in her tracks and turns on Young Guinan.
I am not twelve years old. If I want to go to my quarters and contemplate my situation, it does not mean that I am... pouting.
Okay, okay.

Young Ro turns and continues toward the Turbolift. Young Guinan makes a face at Young Ro's back... then smiles to herself with the simple pleasure of acting like a girl again... then she follows Young Ro.
Young Keiko and O'Brien sit on the couch. There is a long, awkward silence between them as they struggle to make sense of the situation.
I could use a... cup of coffee. How about you?
It's obvious O'Brien's more in need of a distraction than any beverage. He moves to get up, but Young Keiko gestures him back into his chair and walks over to the replicator...
I'll get it. Two coffees... one with cream...
Black... double sweet...
I know. One double sweet.
Young Keiko picks up the two cups of steaming coffee and starts toward O'Brien.
Careful... that's hot...
Miles...
Sorry.

Young Keiko hands him a cup and sits down next to him. A sadness falls over her features... this is a lot to absorb. Young Keiko instinctively cuddles up next to him, looking for comfort. But this has the opposite effect on O'Brien. He stands up... suddenly very uncomfortable with this kind of intimacy.
What's wrong?
It's... I don't know... but this feels wrong, somehow.
Young Keiko stands. Their voices slowly get louder as they grapple with complex emotions.
Miles Edward O'Brien. I am still your wife.
Technically, yes.
Technically?
No. I mean, of course you're my wife... but you're also ten years old.
Beverly said it's actually closer to twelve.
That's not the point.
So what is the point? Is our marriage over?
I didn't say that. But until they find a way to reverse this... this effect... it's going to be hard for me to ignore the fact that you're a little girl.
What if they can't find a way? What if I'm like this the rest of my life? What does that mean for us, for our family?
Mommy?
They both look toward the bedroom. After a beat, they both move to the door.
MOLLY is lying in her bed as O'Brien and Young Keiko ENTER.
What's wrong, Sweetheart?
I want Mommy to read me a story.
All right. What story would you like to hear?
Molly just looks at her.
I want Mommy.
The words knife into Young Keiko and she doesn't know what to do for a moment. O'Brien smoothly moves to his daughter. Young Keiko leaves the room.
What if Daddy reads you a story tonight? Will that be okay?
Molly nods her head.
I'll be right back.
O'Brien EXITS.
Young Keiko is fighting back tears as O'Brien ENTERS.
Keiko...
Young Keiko turns around and buries her head in O'Brien's chest. He comforts her, just as he would any crying twelve year old.
It's going to be all right... I promise... we'll work this out...
She looks up at him.
How?
I don't know.
As O'Brien tries to comfort his wife...
FADE IN:
The ship drops out of warp.

First Officer's Log: Supplemental. The Enterprise has reached the Ligos system, and we have begun to search for the missing Federation science team. Doctor Crusher reports no progress on finding a cure for the members of the shuttle crew.

Young Picard is looking at himself in the mirror, wearing his black T-shirt... staring at the strange, yet familiar face he sees. He turns his head this way and that... touches places under his eyes and around his mouth where only yesterday there were small lines of age. He hesitates for a moment... finally runs a hand through the shock of hair on his head. He grins at the image.
He moves to a chair and picks up his leather jacket and tries it on. The jacket is several sizes too large now and Young Picard can't help but laugh at the comical image of himself in the mirror.
The door CHIMES.
Come.
Troi ENTERS. Young Picard is obviously in good spirits and Troi smiles at the sight of the boy in the man's clothes.
I came to see how you're doing.
I'll have to speak to my tailor, but otherwise I'm well, thank you.
Troi stands beside him and they both examine the way he looks in the mirror.
It's just so... ridiculous. I can't really take myself seriously like this...
He trails off as a new thought occurs to him. The smile on his face dies away and is replaced by a frown. He turns away from the mirror, troubled.
What's wrong?
Beat.
Counselor... if Doctor Crusher can't find a cure... and I have to stay this way... no one's going to take me seriously, are they?

I would say the people who know you, who've worked with you for years, will be able to make the adjustment eventually. But... there are some cultures that would not accept a twelve-year-old captain as a negotiating partner or a credible emissary.
Young Picard takes a long beat to consider this.
In that case, I suppose I'll have to wait until... I grow up again before I'll get another command. That could be ten years... maybe fifteen...
Young Picard mulls this over for a moment... it's a long time.
The question is... what to do until then?
You're still a captain... I'm sure there are other assignments you could be given.
I've spent thirty years of my life aboard starships... I'm not about to sit behind a desk now.
You could return to the Academy... get another degree... brush up on your Latin.

And be Wesley's room-mate, I suppose. I will admit that returning to the Academy does have a certain appeal... but I've always spent my life looking forward... going to the Academy again feels like... looking back.
Troi moves around the room... sees the usual artifacts from Picard's journeys: the Mintakan blanket, Klingon knife, and now the pottery shards from Marlonia.
Then perhaps you could use this time to explore another interest... archeology for instance?
Leave Starfleet?
Not permanently... just a sabbatical. You could spend ten years crawling through caves and digging up artifacts... and still have enough time to become the youngest admiral in Starfleet.
Young Picard moves to the pottery shards and looks down at them.
It would give me a chance to accompany Doctor Langford on her exploration of the ruins on Suvin Four... but to leave the Enterprise...
In a way, you're very lucky. You have a chance do what most people can only dream about... have a second childhood without the pain of growing up.
But Young Picard isn't listening any longer... he's picked up one of the shards of pottery and is turning it over in the light. Troi smiles to herself and quietly EXITS.
Beverly is showing Riker an Okudagram display of some medical information.

This is Captain Picard's rybo-viroxic-nucleic structure from a tissue sample I took this morning. It's the same as a sample I took before the accident -- except it's missing several key viroxic sequences.
I'm afraid it's been a long time since I took genetics, Doctor.

RVN is one of the key factors in our development during puberty. Unlike DNA, which never changes, RVN takes on additional viroxic sequences during adolescence. Those sequences determine how we develop physically. Without them...
We would never mature into adults.
Exactly. Somehow, those key sequences were eliminated in the Captain and the others during transport.
Riker looks at the terminal for a moment.
So what can we do?
There are a couple of options.
Beverly moves over to some SPROUTED SEEDLINGS in petri dishes.
These are the plants Keiko was carrying on the shuttle. Whatever turned the crew into children turned these into seedlings.
Beverly nods and moves to a FLOWERING PLANT identical to the one seen earlier in the shuttlecraft.
We accelerated the growth on one of them, and it developed into a perfectly normal adult plant.
I don't suppose that would work on people.
No... but it does tell us that if we do nothing, they'll probably grow up as they did before.
That's one option...

I do have adult RVN patterns on all four of them. I might be able to send them back through the Transporter pattern buffer and replace the missing sequences... but we can't even attempt that until we know why this happened in the first place. If they were, somehow, to lose more viroxic sequences...
They'd come back even younger.
On their reactions...

What is left of the shuttlecraft is now a lot of junk sitting on the deck of the bay. O'Brien and a few N.D. ENGINEERS are re-assembling the components of the shuttle in some rough order -- like the positioning of debris after a plane crash. O'Brien examines a piece of debris with a tricorder... he then moves it into its proper place on the deck. Geordi ENTERS, carrying a PADD.
I've got the sensor report on the shuttle break-up.
He hands the PADD to O'Brien, who looks at it while Geordi looks over the junk on the floor.
It looks like the break-up began near the starboard bulkhead.
O'Brien nods in agreement.
There are some bulkhead fragments over here.
He leads Geordi to a pile of shattered metal. Geordi bends down to examine some pieces more closely.
My VISOR's picking up torsional stress damage... some micro-fractures... Wait a minute... what's this?
He holds up a ordinary-looking chunk of metal.
Looks like tritanium from the hull.
Yeah... but watch.
As Geordi CRUSHES the metal into DUST with his bare hand.
O'Brien reacts. Geordi peers at the dust in his hand.
It's not tritanium anymore... somehow the molecular structure of the alloy's been changed -- broken down into its constituent elements...
No wonder the bulkhead shattered...
Let's get a sample down to Engineering. I want to run a metallurgical analysis.
As they begin to put some of the dust into a small container...
Young Ro is sitting quietly on the bed, lost in thought. Young Guinan is sitting on a chair, her legs dangling a bit in boredom. Young Guinan lets out a loud sigh. Young Ro ignores her.
Well, this is exciting.
Would you rather be playing with dolls?
I'd rather be doing almost anything other than sitting here and watching you sulk.
Young Guinan gets out of the chair and starts moving around the room, picking up random objects and playing with things.
This isn't some kind of glorious second childhood, Guinan. Our bodies have been violated... changed... doesn't that bother you?
Sure it bothers me, but at the moment I can't do anything about it. So I might as well enjoy it.
Enjoy what? Where did you get the idea that being short and awkward is some kind of wonderful gift?
Young Guinan looks at Young Ro for a beat, then goes over to sit by her on the bed.
There must've been some part of childhood that you didn't loathe. Come on... tell me one happy memory you have.
Look. It was a long, depressing period of my life and I was grateful when it was finally over. I'd rather not relive it.
Young Guinan considers her for a moment.
I bet you were a jumper. A jumper. You know, someone who jumped up and down on furniture all the time.
What?
You were a jumper all right. The quiet ones... they always look so innocent... you think you can turn your back on them... then next thing you know -- bam! They're bouncing on the bed.
Young Ro smiles in disbelief at the outrageous nature of Young Guinan's statement.
That is the most ridiculous thing I've ever heard. Most of the time I didn't even have a bed.
Ah... but you did have one sometimes... and I bet you jumped on it.
I most certainly did not.
Yeah... I can see it in your eyes... you can barely resist the urge to leap up and start jumping around like a Tarkassian razorbeast.
Oh yeah... oh yeah...
Young Guinan suddenly stands up on the bed and starts jumping up and down. Young Ro can't believe this... but she's smiling in spite of herself as the bed is violently shaken underneath her.
This is ridiculous.
That's right... and don't you dare join me, Ro Laren. You don't like jumping on beds!

Young Ro gets off the bed... watches the maniacal jumping of Young Guinan for another beat... her smile grows wider and wider... finally she can't resist any longer and she leaps up and joins in. As the two of them giggle and laugh as they bounce up and down...
Geordi and O'Brien are talking to Riker and Beverly. Geordi gestures to a display of technical information.
We think the shuttle was caught in a molecular reversion field, which caused the structure of the ship to deteriorate. When the field penetrated the hull, it also began to affect the shuttle crew.
When I tried to beam them off, I wasn't able to get a lock because the reversion field was masking part of their patterns.
If the Transporter only registered part of their RVN patterns... that would explain why the key sequences are missing.
Exactly. And without those key sequences, the Transporter reconstructed them as children.
A beat as they consider.
If they're right, will you be able to use the Transporter to reverse the effects?
I think so. As long as there's no reversion field to mask the patterns, we should be able to do it. Chief, can we adjust the molecular imaging scanners to accept --
Bridge to Commander Riker.
Go ahead.
We're entering orbit around Ligos Seven, sir.
On my way. We'll discuss this later.
Riker EXITS.
The Enterprise slows to orbital velocity around Ligos Seven, a planet shrouded in a gaseous atmosphere, wrapped in mystery.
Riker, Worf, and Data at their stations.
Standard orbit, Ensign. Any sign of the science team?
We have been scanning the area since entering the system, but our readings are being disrupted.
Cause?
Extreme fluctuations in the E.M. field.
Riker moves to take a closer look at the console.
However, there is no evidence of relevant stellar or seismic activity which would cause the interference.
Any response to our hails, Mister Worf?
No, sir. I have been attempting to--- Commander, two ships decloaking fore and aft. Klingon birds of prey... B'rel class.
Two BIRDS OF PREY DECLOAK and immediately FIRE on the Enterprise.
Young Picard is looking over the pottery shards under a 24th century microscope when the ship is HIT again. Young Picard instinctively jumps up and heads for the door as the ship goes to RED ALERT.
As before. The ship's condition is RED.
Maximum shields. Take us out of orbit, Ensign. Mister Worf, prepare to return fire...
And the ship SHUDDERS from another direct HIT...
FADE IN:
As before. The ship is ROCKED by another blast.
Damage report.
We've lost primary life-support. Switching to secondary systems.
Lock phasers on target bearing to port.
Phasers locked.
Fire.
PHASER FIRE hits a Klingon ship, but the ship is protected by its shields.
As before.
Minor damage to one ship. Its shields are holding.
The ship is ROCKED again.
Starboard power coupling is down... warp engines off-line.
Shields?
Down to thirteen percent.
The Enterprise is struck by the torpedoes from both Klingon ships.
As the Enterprise recoils from the impact...
Casualties reported on decks twenty-six and twenty-seven...
Sensors and secondary generators off-line... life support down to sixty-seven percent...
Engineering, status report.
Intercut as needed with:
Geordi at the computer consoles...
Their last shots took out auxiliary power and emergency back-ups. It'll take at least an hour to get warp power back on-line.
As before.
We've lost shields. Heavy casualties on decks thirty-five through forty.
I am detecting Transporter signatures in three cargo bays. We are being boarded.

Young Picard is running down a corridor toward a Turbolift. He arrives at the Turbolift and the doors OPEN -- but Young Picard pulls up short as an ARMED FERENGI comes out of the Turbolift and points the weapon at Young Picard. He's been caught.
Geordi is in his office. He hears the SOUND of phaser FIRE and comes running out, but it's too late -- TWO FERENGI have him and his men covered by their weapons.
As before.
Initiate intruder alert. All security teams to proceed to --
Riker suddenly turns at the SOUND of a Transporter Beam-in.
TWO FERENGI, BERIK and MORTA, MATERIALIZE on the Bridge with alien rifles drawn...
Put down your weapons.
Worf draws his phaser and FIRES as he dives for cover, but misses...
The Ferengi loosen a couple of BLASTS at Worf and Data, HITTING them both.
Hits the deck and rolls out of the way of a phaser BLAST. He quickly hits his combadge.
Computer, deactivate all command functions. Authorization, Riker-Omega-Three...
All command functions suspended.
All Bridge consoles DE-ACTIVATE as TWO MORE FERENGI, armed with alien rifles, ENTER from two Turbolift.
This is Morta. We have secured the Bridge. Begin transporting all able-bodied adults to the surface.
A FERENGI is guarding O'Brien, who is now a prisoner. As the doors open, FERENGI Guards herd more Adult Crew Members (among them, Geordi) into the room...
Riker is standing off to one side, under guard. Worf and Data are still unconscious on the deck. Berik and Morta are trying to work one of the aft consoles, but are having no success.
They have locked out the command functions.
You said they would not have time.
You led the assault team, you were too slow.
You dare to blame me!
But before they can carry this any further, the Turbolift doors OPEN and DAIMON LURIN ENTERS. Morta and Berik quickly move to him.
We have secured the ship, Daimon, but Morta's incompetence has denied us access to---
My incompetence! Daimon, you know that I am --
Enough. Where is the Captain of this ship?
Berik looks to Riker.
I'm in command of this vessel. Who are you and on whose authority do you --

I am Daimon Lurin and I now declare this ship to be a loss and open to claim according to the Ferengi Salvage Code. You will cooperate with our salvage operations or we will begin executing your crew.
Off Riker's expression...
FADE IN:
The Enterprise is re-entering orbit, with a Bird of Prey nearby.

Young Ro, Young Guinan, Young Keiko, and SEVERAL N.D. CHILDREN are in the school room. The real kids are jabbering to each other with concern... there is an edge of fear in the air and it wouldn't take much more to turn this scene into hysteria.

The doors OPEN and Young Picard ENTERS, escorted by Berik. He gives Young Picard a shove into the room and then posts himself outside the door in the Corridor, before closing the door. Young Ro, Young Guinan, and Young Keiko go immediately to Young Picard.
Is everyone all right?
No fatalities or injuries among the children. The Ferengi have control of Main Engineering and decks twenty-three through thirty-seven.
We have to assume they've also taken the Bridge.
Captain... do you know what they've done with the younger children... with my little girl?
They're taking all the adults down to the surface. It looks like they're keeping all the children on board the ship. Where was your daughter?
In primary care on deck fourteen.
Young Picard guides them over to a table with a computer terminal.
We need to regain control of the ship. Options?
We could flood the ship with anesthizine gas.
That's locked out along with the rest of the command functions.
If they're typical Ferengi, they're probably very pleased with themselves about now... maybe even getting a little overconfident.
Agreed. They might not think they need much of their crew to hold the ship. We could use the element of surprise to give ourselves a tactical advantage...
Tactical advantage... ? Jean-Luc... look at your team for a minute. We're children.
We can't just stay here while our ship is being commandeered.
I'm not suggesting that we do. But we can't act as if we were still adults.
What do you suggest?
We look like children. Maybe it's time we started acting like children.
Off their reactions...
Daimon Lurin is making himself comfortable in Picard's chair, as Riker ENTERS. (We see a Ferengi guard just outside the door).
I hope your profit margin is pretty high on this little adventure, Lurin... because you're risking war with the Federation.

We're not affiliated with the Ferengi Alliance. We're... in business for ourselves. And yes, it will be highly profitable. For an investment of two surplus Klingon ships... a few repairs... and some weapons... we've netted a Federation starship and her crew, not to mention a planet rich in Vendarite.
So that's what this is all about. What did you do with the science team that was on the surface?
They have proved most... helpful in extracting the mineral.
You made them slave laborers.

The addition of your crew will greatly speed up the process. As for your ship... I'm sure it will fetch a handsome price on the Romulan market. But before that can happen, we need to regain access to your central computer.
You don't really think I'm going to help you.
Lurin fixes him with a steely look.
I think... that the mines on Ligos Seven can be very hazardous. How many people in your crew?
One thousand, fourteen.
Lurin holds his gaze for a moment.
Very hazardous, Commander.
Lurin EXITS, leaving Riker with something to think about.
Young Ro and Young Keiko are taking apart a small section of bulkhead at one end of the room.
Young Picard and Young Guinan are at the desktop computer terminal seen earlier.
Young Picard activates the school-room terminal. Because this is the school room, a DIFFERENT Computer Voice than the one we're used to hearing responds when he turns on the terminal.
Hello. I'm the classroom computer system. What can I do for you, today?
Computer, display interior security grid.
I'm sorry, but I can't do that. Would you like to play a game?
No, I would not. Computer, display an internal schematic diagram.
I'm sorry, but I can't do that. Would you like to see some interesting animals?
Young Picard glares at the screen in frustration, but Young Guinan intercedes.
It's a child's computer, remember? Computer, can you show me a picture of the inside of the Enterprise?

A BRIGHTLY COLORED diagram of the Enterprise comes up on the screen. NOTE: this should not be one of our standard schematics. It should be a children's version of a ship diagram, with greatly simplified graphics and brightly colored designs.
The Enterprise is a Galaxy-class starship. Do you know how to spell Enterprise? E -- N -- T Delete audio.
The Voice STOPS.

All right, this will have to do... we're here... there's a service conduit that runs from here to here and then connects to a Jeffries Tube here... but you and Ensign Ro will still have to cross this corridor before you can get to Main Engineering.
Young Guinan studies the display.
She manages to pull the final Mees panel away from the bulkhead, revealing a Jeffries Tube behind the wall.
Captain...
Young Picard and Young Guinan come over.
Excellent. Ready? Make it so.
Young Guinan and Young Ro EXIT to the Jeffries Tube.

As a TOY suddenly bumps up against Young Picard's leg. Alexander comes running up, carrying a remote control PADD and looking apologetic. The toy looks like a cross between a lunch-box and a spider, with several odd-looking armatures poking out from the sides. There are no apparent wheels, but it glides along the floor.
I'm sorry... Captain.

Alexander moves the toy away from Young Picard and begins playing with it again by using the remote control. As Young Picard watches the toy glide across the floor, he begins to get an idea. He goes to Alexander.
Alexander, would you mind if I... borrowed your toy for a little while?
Go ahead.
Thank you.
He hands the remote to Young Picard, who takes it and then EXITS to the tube along with Young Keiko.
The ship is in orbit.
FERENGI #1 is standing behind the console. The doors OPEN and the toy seen earlier ENTERS the room. The Ferengi looks at it in puzzlement for a moment... then the toy EXITS again.
The Ferengi waits a beat... then decides to follow it... he EXITS.
The Ferengi ENTERS from the Transporter Room just in time to see the toy disappear around the corner. He follows it.
As the Ferengi turns the corner, Young Picard and Young Keiko peek around the corner and then quickly EXIT to the Transporter Room.

Young Picard -- carrying the remote control seen earlier -- and Young Keiko ENTER. Young Keiko moves quickly to the storage lockers on the far side of the room while Young Picard moves to the Transporter Console and starts to rapidly enter information into the console. Young Keiko opens the locker and removes several PHASERS.
The remote control PADD Young Picard is carrying suddenly BEEPS.
He's picked up the toy.
Young Picard rapidly finishes his work and Young Keiko closes the locker, with several phasers in her arms. They run OUT the doors.
A few beats pass and then Ferengi #1 ENTERS, carrying the toy. He sets the toy aside in irritation and then turns his back on it.
From this angle, we can now see that there is a COMBADGE attached to it.
The Ferengi continues his solitary watch.
Young Ro and Young Guinan are moving quickly down the tube on their hands and knees.
This is the first time these Jeffries tubes haven't seemed cramped.
How much farther do we have to go?
About fifty meters... don't tell me you're tired.
I'm not as young as I used to be.
Young Ro stops and they look at each other for a beat.
FERENGI #2 is on guard duty here... but he's pretty bored at this point and is sitting at Beverly's desk, toying with some of the items on the desk.
Suddenly Alexander ENTERS from the Corridor doors. He creeps up to the glass window and then taps on the glass before running back out into the Corridor.
Ferengi #2 whirls around, but doesn't see anything. He immediately gets up and heads for the Corridor.

As the Ferengi EXITS to the Corridor... Alexander ENTERS from the other door to Sickbay. He quickly moves to a storage bin and begins pulling out hyposprays. Once he has as many as he can carry, he runs back OUT of the room.
Young Ro and Young Guinan come scrambling down the tube.
They both stop...
This is it. Main Engineering. Now we wait.
Alexander comes scrambling out of the Jeffries Tube, with hyposprays. Young Picard and Young Keiko are there to meet them.
Report.
Mission accomplished, sir. The one in Sickbay never saw me.
Alexander hands the hyposprays to Young Picard, who in turn, hands one to Young Keiko.
Very good.
I'd say we're ready. Have you figured out how to get to the Bridge?
Young Picard frowns... he's definitely not looking forward to this.
I'm afraid I can only think of one way...
Berik is still standing guard in the Corridor outside the school room. The doors OPEN and Young Picard ENTERS the corridor. Berik levels his phaser at him.
What do you want?
Young Picard adopts a petulant little boy attitude.
I need to see my father.
Go back inside.
I need to see him right now.
Do not argue with me. Go back inside.
I need him now! Now! Now! Now!
Berik grabs him by the shoulder, but Young Picard pulls away and pretends to be hurt.
You hurt me! I want my father! I want my father!
Berik doesn't know how to react to this screaming child... finally gives in.
All right. Just stop that.
He grabs Young Picard and hauls him to the Turbolift.
Riker is staring outside, deep in thought. The door suddenly OPENS and Berik ENTERS, dragging the red-eyed Young Picard...
Here he is. Now be quiet!
What's going on?
Daddy!
He runs across the room and directly into Riker's arms. On Number One's astonished reaction...
FADE IN:
Young Picard and "Dad" Riker sit together at the table while Berik keeps a watchful eye on them. As Young Picard stares up at Riker...
So... son. How are you?
I'm okay.
And what about your friends... Keiko and Guinan and Ro?
They're okay too. But...
He sighs, pretends to be sad about something.
What's wrong?
We don't have anything to do... none of the games are working.
A look between the two of them.
I know. The Ferengi made Daddy turn off the main computer.
Can't you just turn on the kid's computer in Schoolroom Eight? We just want to play a few games.
I don't know if they'll let me do that, Jean-Luc, but I'll ask.
Thanks, Number One.
Berik's head snaps around at this un-sonlike response. But Young Picard quickly catches himself.
He's my Number One Daddy.
Riker and Young Picard both glance at Berik... and realize that they better make this look good. They both awkwardly stand and stiffly hug each other in imitation of father and son.
Alexander and the other children wait with Young Keiko. Suddenly the doors open and Young Picard is shoved INTO the room by Berik.
How did it go?
He understood. We should have access very soon.
Lurin is peering at Picard's fish with interest... he gropes about with his hand, looking for a way to reach inside. The door CHIMES.
Come in.
Riker, escorted by Morta, ENTERS. Lurin's eyes narrow and he gives Riker an evil smile.
I understand your... son was here to see you.
That's right.
We Ferengi do not bring our offspring along with us aboard ships.
Then I suppose that's your loss. We consider our families to be one of our strengths.
I think you will find they can also be a weakness. Unless you release the computer to our control, I will execute every child on this ship... beginning with yours.
Riker appears outraged.
Even you aren't that cruel.

Riker takes a step toward Lurin, but Morta jabs the phaser in his back and he stops. A tense moment... then Riker's bravado seems to collapse into weariness and resignation.
All right... all right... just don't harm my son.

Vorcha-doh-baghK... Kahless.
Off the look on Kahless' face.

Q'apla, son of Mogh.

Koral.
